pages.text: A curve made of many small chances is the $(thing)normal distribution$(): f(x) = e^(−(x−μ)²/2σ²)/(σ√2π). 68% of it lies within one width of its centre, 95% within two.

Bayes' rule turns a belief into a better one: P(H|E) = P(E|H)·P(H)/P(E). A check that is 99% reliable, for something one person in a hundred has, is right only one time in six when it says yes - because most yeses are false alarms among the many who do not have it.

The $(item)Bayesian Analyzer$() combines a $(item)Prior Tablet$() with evidence into a $(item)Posterior Tablet$(). Carry Posterior Tablets while solving research derivations: each one pays for a hint instead of Insight.
